newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, UK agree need to boost air links.
newsitem.headline: Russia, UK agree need to boost air links.

text.p: Russia and Britain agreed on Tuesday on the need to boost air links as a means of strengthening economic and trade ties.

Foreign Secretary Robin Cook discussed the request by British Airways Plc and other British airlines to expand their flights to Moscow and Russia's regions as part of a new bilateral air services agreement.
BA, which already flies to Moscow and St Petersburg wants to add flights to Ekaterinburg, Samara and Rostov.
Talks on the agreement are due to resume later this year, and Cook and Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov agreed they must not be allowed to get bogged down.
"There needs to be a push on air services," a British official said after the talks.
BA chairman Sir Colin Marshall will get the chance to make his case when he leads a delegation of British businessmen to Moscow in mid-September for talks with Nemtsov and others.

Cook said Britain was keen to boost trade with Russia and expressed strong support for the economic liberalisation measures that Nemtsov and other reformers in President Boris Yeltsin's government are driving through.

"In particular we are anxious to look at how we can assist the training of managers for Russia, particularly through education in Britain, where we have some excellent business schools," Cook told reporters.
He told Nemtsov that he would look at how this could be done under the umbrella of Britain's "Know How Fund", which promotes economic reform in former communist countries.

The two also discussed how Britain, during its six-month stint as president of the European Union, starting in January, could help strengthen ties between the EU and Russia and help remove barriers to trade.

"I want to see a Russia that is able to play its full part, diplomatically and politically, in the international community and I also want a relationship between Russia and Britain in which we are able to expand our economic cooperation to our mutual advantage," Cook said.
